note: Wooded Ozark-border hills in Warren County south of Pendleton, with a 6.5-mile multi-use trail open to hikers, bikes and horses. Four primitive camping spots, each beside a small gravel parking lot on the edge roads; no facilities. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: four map-designated camping spots at perimeter gravel lots; pin on the north lot (GIS 173). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches; not waterfront kept. The page's bare 'Camping is prohibited.' line is the known page artifact.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Designated Camping Sites, Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted in spots designated on the area map'; the 2022 map has four 'Primitive Camping' symbols, each beside a parking lot (north, west off Route B, east off Route EE, south off Low Gap Road). Rule 140 carries the standard text followed by a bare 'Camping is prohibited.' line - the known page artifact (camping is listed under Things to Do). No special-use-only rule, no Rule 101.

PIN fine: stored 38.79708,-91.28136 = GIS 27 point 173, on the south edge of the north gravel lot (lot 1013, 14 m) beside the road - a small lot (~25 x 20 m) that a 23-ft rig can turn in. The west spot (371, off Route B) is beside lot 1016 at an old field edge.
CLUSTERS: the four spots are 2.1-4.6 km apart, each a single small lot on its own road - none qualifies for a split.
HORSES: no horse camp; the 6.5-mile 'Hiking/Biking/Equestrian Trail' is open to horses (closed to horses in firearms deer season and spring turkey shooting hours).
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept (upland lot; no water near).
PHONE: 'For more information call (636) 456-3368' matches stored.
